solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Cuckoo grips twig (5)

indicatorNotes.Cuckoo: cuckoo is slang for crazy, and letters that have gone crazy scramble themselves

annotation.surface: A cuckoo clutches a twig in its claws.
annotation.walkthrough: Cuckoo looks like the bird doing the gripping, but here it is the adjective meaning crazy.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a small shoot snapped from a plant, like a sprig of parsley, is a little twig.

entries.clue: Splinter group determined to welcome Conservative (4)

indicatorNotes.to welcome: a host who welcomes a guest takes them inside, so SET takes in C

annotation.surface: A breakaway faction is resolved to take in a Tory member.
annotation.walkthrough: C for Conservative is the usual abbreviation for the British Tory party, which fits the political surface.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a sect is a group that has broken away from a larger religious or political body.

entries.clue: Raised berth space (4)

indicatorNotes.Raised: in a down clue, raising a word lifts its bottom letter to the top, so it reads upward

blocks.note: to moor a boat is to berth it

annotation.surface: A bunk bed set high up to free some floor space.
annotation.walkthrough: Berth looks like a noun (a bed on a ship or train), but it is the verb for tying up a boat.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the sense of room to move or no room left: available space.

entries.clue: With aim to grasp information technology, I work solo (2,2,5)

indicatorNotes.to grasp: to grasp something is to hold it in your hand, so GOAL closes around IT

blocks.note: IT is the usual short form
I is the Roman numeral one

annotation.surface: Someone keen to master computing decides to learn it without help.
annotation.walkthrough: The I looks like the subject of 'work solo', but it belongs to the wordplay as ONE.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: to go it alone is to do something by yourself, without help or partners.

entries.clue: Puzzled finding flightless birds in garden plot (7)

indicatorNotes.in: the birds are placed in the plot, so their letters sit inside BED

blocks.note: emus are large Australian birds that cannot fly

annotation.surface: A gardener is baffled to discover ostrich-like birds among the vegetables.
annotation.walkthrough: Garden plot is a crossword favourite for BED; plot alone could suggest a storyline.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: someone bemused is bewildered and cannot make sense of what is happening.

entries.clue: Book dragged leaving learner irritated (6)

indicatorNotes.leaving: something leaving a word walks out of it, so L departs from LUGGED

blocks.note: B is the standard abbreviation for book
L for learner, as on British L-plates

annotation.surface: A reader was annoyed at having to haul a heavy book around.
annotation.walkthrough: L for learner comes from the L-plates new drivers display in Britain.
annotation.definitionFit: Informal synonym: something that bugs you gets on your nerves, so bugged means annoyed.

entries.clue: Infuriated when barrier gets erected (3)

indicatorNotes.gets erected: erecting something stands it upright, so in a down clue the word reads from the bottom up

blocks.note: a dam is a barrier across a river

annotation.surface: Someone is furious that a fence has gone up next door.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a neighbour's fence; the barrier needed is one across a river.
annotation.definitionFit: Informal sense: mad in everyday speech often means angry rather than insane.

entries.clue: Horse half ignored by stalking cat (8)

indicatorNotes.half ignored: ignoring half of a word leaves the other half, so STALKING keeps STAL

blocks.note: a lion is a big cat

annotation.surface: A horse goes half-unnoticed by a big cat hunting it.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Stalking cat' reads as a lion on the hunt; the two words give separate pieces.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by class: a stallion is a particular kind of horse, the uncastrated male.

entries.clue: Use symptoms to identify disorder in sea dog (8)

indicatorNotes.disorder: letters in disorder are out of order, so IN SEA DOG is jumbled

annotation.surface: A ship's doctor works out what illness an old sailor has.
annotation.walkthrough: Disorder poses as the illness to be identified, but it is the instruction to rearrange; a sea dog is an old sailor.
annotation.definitionFit: A descriptive definition: doctors diagnose by reading symptoms and naming the condition behind them.

entries.clue: Celtic ultimately not winning final (7)

indicatorNotes.ultimately: ultimately means in the end, so take the end letter of Celtic

annotation.surface: Celtic end up beaten in a cup final.
annotation.walkthrough: Celtic is a Glasgow football club, which makes 'final' look like a match rather than an adjective.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: closing remarks or the closing stages are the final ones.

entries.clue: Regularly seen admiral near woman (5)

indicatorNotes.Regularly seen: something seen regularly turns up at even intervals, so take every other letter

blocks.note: the second, fourth, sixth, eighth and tenth letters

annotation.surface: An admiral is often spotted with a lady by his side.
annotation.walkthrough: Crosswords often define a first name just as 'woman' or 'girl'.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: Diana is one of many women's names, so any woman could be one.

entries.clue: Fruit transported to new realm (10)

indicatorNotes.transported: transported things are moved to new positions, so the letters are rearranged

annotation.surface: Produce is shipped off to a far-off land.
annotation.walkthrough: Transported sounds like shipping the fruit, but it is the instruction to rearrange the letters.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by class: the watermelon is one kind of fruit.

entries.clue: Coat guy wrapped around poorly prime minister (9)

indicatorNotes.wrapped around: wrapping something around goes outside it, so MAN encloses ILL

annotation.surface: A man wraps his coat around a leader who is feeling unwell.
annotation.walkthrough: Harold Macmillan was British prime minister from 1957 to 1963; mac is British for a raincoat.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: Harold Macmillan is one of the UK's past prime ministers.

entries.clue: Likely for newborn to consume liquids primarily (8)

indicatorNotes.to consume: whatever you consume goes inside you, so BABE takes L in
indicatorNotes.primarily: primarily means first of all, so take the first letter of liquids

annotation.surface: A new baby will probably take mostly fluids.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Likely for newborn' reads as one phrase, but for is PRO and likely stands alone as the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: what is probable is likely to happen or be true.

entries.clue: Simplicity of some ideas, in essence (8)

indicatorNotes.some: some of the following words means only part of their letters, taken in a run

annotation.surface: Good ideas are, at heart, simple.
annotation.walkthrough: In essence sounds like a summary, but its letters carry the end of the answer; the comma is ignored.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the easiness of a task is its simplicity.

entries.clue: I’m unsure backing a relative’s cause (6)

indicatorNotes.backing: backing means moving backwards, so ER is written in reverse

blocks.note: er is the noise of someone hesitating

annotation.surface: Someone hesitates over supporting a family member's campaign.
annotation.walkthrough: Backing looks like support for the cause, and the ’s stands for 'is', joining wordplay to definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the reason for something is its cause.

entries.clue: With sides leaving, game with netted sticks is over (6)

indicatorNotes.With sides leaving: a word's sides are its two ends, so they depart from LACROSSE

blocks.note: lacrosse is played with sticks that have a net at the end

annotation.surface: The teams walk off and the lacrosse match is finished.
annotation.walkthrough: Over reads as 'finished', but it is the definition in the sense of from one side to the other.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in one sense: to walk over the bridge is to walk across it.

entries.clue: Threaten mischievous sprite with death (6)

blocks.note: an imp is a small mischievous spirit

annotation.surface: An impish creature menaces someone with killing.
annotation.walkthrough: Threaten here is intransitive, as danger threatens or looms, not as one person threatens another.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: something impending hangs over you, about to happen, just as a storm threatens.

entries.clue: Wedding helper’s offer to accommodate trips with mother (10)

indicatorNotes.to accommodate: to accommodate guests is to take them in, so BID houses RIDES and MA

annotation.surface: A wedding helper offers to put up a mother on her travels.
annotation.walkthrough: The ’s stands for 'is', linking the definition to the wordplay rather than marking possession.
annotation.definitionFit: A descriptive definition: a bridesmaid attends the bride and helps her on the wedding day.

entries.clue: Revolution advanced to north state (4)

indicatorNotes.to north: north is up on a map, so in a down clue the letters read upward

blocks.note: rev is short for a revolution of an engine
A is the abbreviation for advanced, as in A-level

annotation.surface: An uprising pushes on towards a northern state.
annotation.walkthrough: State looks like a country's region, but it is the verb meaning declare; revolution is the engine sense, not an uprising.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym of the verb: to aver is to state something as fact.

entries.clue: Begrudge emissary forgetting nothing (4)

indicatorNotes.forgetting: what you forget goes missing, so the O drops out of ENVOY

annotation.surface: Someone resents a diplomat who has achieved nothing.
annotation.walkthrough: Nothing is O, the zero-shaped letter, a common crossword swap.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to envy or begrudge someone is to resent their good fortune.

entries.clue: Sound from animal left in pound (5)

indicatorNotes.in: what is left in the pound is inside it, so L sits within BEAT

annotation.surface: Noise from a creature abandoned in the animal pound.
annotation.walkthrough: Pound looks like an animal shelter, but it is the verb meaning beat.
annotation.definitionFit: A descriptive definition: a bleat is the cry a sheep or goat makes.

entries.clue: Hill degenerate climbs (3)

indicatorNotes.climbs: a climber goes up, so in a down clue the word reads from the bottom

blocks.note: to rot is to decay, degenerate

annotation.surface: A disreputable person scrambles up a hillside.
annotation.walkthrough: Degenerate reads as a noun for a bad person; it is the verb. Tors are the rocky hilltops of places like Dartmoor in England.
annotation.definitionFit: A regional word: in south-west England a tor is a rocky hill.

entries.clue: Rouse characters held back by an evil nemesis (7)

indicatorNotes.characters held: characters are letters, and these ones are held within the words that follow
indicatorNotes.back: back means the letters are read in reverse

annotation.surface: A hero is stirred into action but held back by a wicked arch-enemy.
annotation.walkthrough: Characters looks like people in a story, but it means letters.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to enliven a party is to rouse it, giving it more life.

entries.clue: Made certain knight reused battered shields (7)

indicatorNotes.battered: something battered is knocked out of shape, so REUSED is rearranged
indicatorNotes.shields: a shield covers what it protects, so the jumbled letters go around N

blocks.note: N for knight, as in chess notation

annotation.surface: A knight checked that his recycled, dented shields would do.
annotation.walkthrough: Shields looks like a knight's kit, but it is the verb for going around N.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to ensure something is to make certain it happens.

entries.clue: Residing in New York, concerned with turning very anxious (5)

indicatorNotes.Residing in: a resident lives inside a place, so the letters sit inside NY
indicatorNotes.turning: turning round reverses direction, so RE becomes ER

annotation.surface: A New York resident preoccupied with change is very jittery.
annotation.walkthrough: Very looks like it intensifies anxious, but it is just the letter V.
annotation.definitionFit: A British sense: nervy means jumpy or anxious, though in America it can mean cheeky.
